messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — seeing recurring NVIDIA Xid 13 and Xid 31 on a small cohort of p4d nodes in us-west-2 over the last 18h. Patterns look tied to long-context infer jobs (gpt-medium-v1).
Chris Patel: Can you paste the dmesg / nvidia-smi snippet? Which GPUs/nodes exactly?
Maria Chen: Quick dump from node gpu-p4d-127 (just filtered):
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=4234, thu=0
[ 12346.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=4234
[ 12350.234567] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=7890
```
Maria Chen: nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ECC on that GPU: 
```
GPU 0: GPU-SN-7C24
    FB Memory Usage : 32412 MiB / 40960 MiB
    ECC Errors
        Volatile:  corrected=142  uncorrected=0
        Aggregate: corrected=142  uncorrected=0
```
Dave Nguyen: Looks like corrected ECC growth on that card. Xid 13 tends to be ECC/corruption, 31 is typically illegal/invalid memory access during a kernel. The corrected ECC rate is suspicious (142). Could be flaky DIMM or intermittent thermal issue.
Silvia Romero: I queried telemetry by request header (X-Request-Id) to correlate model + seq_len + GPU node. SQL: 
```
SELECT model, avg(seq_len) as avg_seq, count(*) as calls, sum(case when xid is not null then 1 else 0 end) as xid_count
FROM inference_events
WHERE node = 'gpu-p4d-127' AND ts > now() - interval '24 hours'
GROUP BY model
ORDER BY xid_count desc
```
Silvia Romero: Result: gpt-medium-v1 — avg_seq 4.1k, calls 1248, xid_count 27. Smaller models had 0-1 xid each.
Chris Patel: Good correlation. Any thermal throttling in node metrics?
Maria Chen: Node metrics show repeated short spikes to 82-84C on GPU core during long requests, but fan duty at 100% reported. No sustained TDR / reset in dmesg besides Xid messages.
ops-bot: [AUTO] gpu-p4d-127 reported 3 Xid events in 30m window; flagged for investigator.
Dave Nguyen: Plan options: (A) drain+replace card (safe, needs spare P4d in us-west-2) (B) repro with stress test and vendor diagnostics (run cuMemtest / ECC stress) (C) migrate high-seq workloads to another region / instance type while we iterate.
Silvia Romero: We're low on spare p4d capacity in us-west-2 this week — moving production workloads is costly. Suggest attempt repro and short drain (cordon node) to run vendor diag first.
Chris Patel: Agreed. Steps: 1) cordon node, 2) repro with controlled load (seq_len ~4k), 3) capture pmon, dmesg, nv-hostengine logs, 4) if Xid reproduces, escalate to vendor and schedule RMA/replacement.
Maria Chen: I'll cordon and schedule repro in the 02:00-04:00 UTC maintenance window. Commands I'll run: 
```bash
kubectl cordon gpu-p4d-127
kubectl drain gpu-p4d-127 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
# run repro container for ~2h: docker run --gpus all redwood/testing:gpu-stress --model gpt-medium-v1 --seq 4000 --concurrency 2
# capture traces
dmesg | grep -i "Xid" -n > /tmp/xid.log
nvidia-smi pmon -s um -c 100 > /tmp/pmon.log &
```
Dave Nguyen: If repro is flaky, also run memtest: `cuda-memtest --runs=10 --gpu=0` and log ECC deltas pre/post.
Silvia Romero: I'll open a vendor ticket with serial GPU-SN-7C24 if we see consistent Xid after repro. Also assign ops-bot to annotate node history so replacements are traceable.
Maria Chen: Quick note — some earlier incidents with Xid 13 were resolved by updating driver from 525.85 to 535.x because of a kernel interaction; what driver is on this node?
Chris Patel: Driver is 525.85.10. Good catch. Could do a staged driver upgrade on a repro node. But vendor RMA still possible if memtest shows hardware errors.
Dave Nguyen: Decision: do repro + memtest + driver bump on a spare repro node; if reproducible post-driver bump, escalate RMA. If non-repro, leave cordoned and requeue workloads to other nodes and monitor.
ops-bot: [ACTION] Maria Chen assigned -> run repro + collect logs. Silvia Romero assigned -> open vendor ticket if repro confirms.
Maria Chen: Will update thread after repro run tonight. :eyes:
